One-line judgment: this line of work is not filling in a template, but writing, modifying and testing the code and scripts that make computer applications run, working from specifications written by software and web developers or other staff, and possibly developing programs that store and locate and retrieve specific documents and data. O*NET defines the occupation as creating, modifying and testing the code and scripts that allow computer applications to run; working from specifications drawn up by software and web developers or other individuals; and possibly developing and writing computer programs to store, locate and retrieve specific documents and data; its tasks are led by writing and analyzing and reviewing and rewriting programs using workflow charts and diagrams and applying knowledge of computer capabilities and subject matter and symbolic logic and correcting errors by making appropriate changes and then rechecking the program to ensure the desired results are produced, and this page is developed on the precise occupational scope of O*NET-SOC 15-1251.00.

The work of computer programmers can be divided into three linked but independent work dimensions. The first is requirements clarification and solutions and documentation: communicate with management and engineering and technical staff to clarify program intent and identify problems and propose changes; write and analyze and review and rewrite programs, using workflow charts and diagrams and applying knowledge of computer capabilities and subject matter and symbolic logic; prepare detailed workflow charts and diagrams that describe input and output and logical operation and convert them into a series of instructions written in a computer language; write documentation for program development and subsequent revisions and insert comments in code instructions so others can understand them; and write or contribute to instructions or manuals to guide end users. The second is coding and debugging and validation: correct errors by making appropriate changes and then rechecking the program to ensure the desired results are produced; perform or direct revisions and repair and expansion of existing programs to increase operating efficiency or adapt to new requirements; write and update and maintain computer programs or software packages that handle specific tasks (such as inventory tracking and data access or controlling other equipment); trial run programs and software applications to confirm they produce the required information and the instructions are correct; and troubleshoot whether networks and workstations and system central processing units or peripherals respond to program instructions. The third is collaboration and system support and people and user support: consult with computer operators or systems analysts and assist them in defining and resolving problems in program operation; perform systems analysis and programming tasks as a systems programmer to maintain and control the use of computer system software; assign and coordinate and review the work and activities of programmers; train subordinates in programming and coding; develop websites; train users to use and understand computer programs; and collaborate with computer manufacturers and other users to develop new programming methods.

Six recurring occupational judgments: whether the specification and inputs and outputs and boundaries are read to an implementable level; whether the design is consistent with existing structure and interfaces; whether error handling and exception paths are covered; whether validation is reproducible and includes regression; whether commits and review and release follow the process; and whether comments and documentation are updated to a handover-ready level.
Judgment one: whether the specification and inputs and outputs and boundaries are read to an implementable level

Turn the specification into a clear list of inputs and outputs and constraints and boundary conditions and exception scenarios; confirm ambiguous or contradictory points with the specification owner first and keep records; do not substitute unfounded practices such as writing to my own understanding first and sorting it out once it runs for clarification.
Judgment two: whether the design is consistent with existing structure and interfaces

Read the existing code and interfaces and data models and naming and layering conventions before starting; reuse existing capabilities rather than building a separate set; explain the scope of impact for new dependencies and interface changes and have the relevant parties confirm.
Judgment three: whether error handling and exception paths are covered

Write explicit handling and prompts for null values and out-of-range and timeout and concurrency and external dependency failures; distinguish recoverable from unrecoverable errors and give log and alert levels; do not swallow exceptions or mask problems with hardcoded fallbacks.
Judgment four: whether validation is reproducible and includes regression

Write reproducible validation steps or use cases for the change and keep the execution results; confirm that existing functionality still works after regression; for parts that cannot be validated automatically, write out the manual validation steps and criteria.
Judgment five: whether commits and review and release follow the process

Submit according to the employer's review and branching and merge and release process and respond to review comments; confirm permissions and approvals for changes involving data and credentials and configuration; do not bypass review to go directly into production.
Judgment six: whether comments and documentation are updated to a handover-ready level

Write key assumptions and boundaries and known limitations into comments and documentation; update workflow diagrams and user manuals and handover notes in step; let the colleague taking over understand and run and modify the program from the documentation.

The six directions share some capabilities with this occupation: reading specifications and reading code, validating with reproducible steps, submitting and keeping records according to the process, and communicating with stakeholders. The real difference lies in the scope of responsibility: this occupation focuses on writing and testing and maintaining code and scripts according to an established specification; the management direction focuses on people and budget and delivery; the systems analysis direction focuses on business solution conversion; the research direction focuses on algorithm and model innovation; the support direction focuses on user and desktop support; the network architecture direction focuses on end-to-end network design and capacity planning; the testing direction focuses on quality systems and test engineering. When choosing, it is suggested to first verify with a deliverable exercise of reading specifications — breaking down boundaries — writing code — use case validation — fixing defects, rather than comparing titles first.

The comparison is based on the occupational definition and 17 tasks and work activities and work context descriptions on the O*NET-SOC 15-1251.00 page, the related and adjacent occupation codes listed there, the adjacent occupation slug list registered in this evidence route (computer-and-information-systems-managers, computer-systems-analysts, computer-and-information-research-scientists, computer-support-specialists, computer-network-architects), and public occupational materials for each adjacent occupation; this evidence route also registers the Mainland China computer programmer occupational standard (4-04-05-01), which can be used to explain the China skill boundary but is not equated with the U.S. scope; the comparison is editorial synthesis and does not constitute a software security, compliance or legal conclusion.

The table below compares roles and occupations adjacent to this occupation: computer and information systems managers, computer systems analysts, computer and information research scientists, computer support specialists, computer network architects, and the software quality assurance and testing direction. The four columns each answer the same kind of question: what this direction does, where the key difference from this occupation lies, and what kind of person is better suited to choosing it.

Computer and information systems managers are responsible for the people and budget and project and delivery coordination of the information technology department and do not carry coding and debugging of specific modules; this occupation focuses on writing and testing code according to an established specification.
People willing to coordinate department people and budget and delivery suit that direction; people willing to do code implementation and debugging and validation suit this occupation.
Mainly department plans and budgets and delivery and operations records.
Computer and information systems managers

Computer systems analysts focus on translating business requirements into system solutions and coordinating them and usually do not carry long-term coding and maintenance; this occupation takes turning a specification into a reliable implementation as its object.
People willing to do requirements analysis and solution coordination suit that direction; people willing to do coding and debugging and documentation suit this occupation.
Mainly requirements and solutions and implementation coordination records.
Computer systems analysts

Computer and information research scientists focus on algorithm and model research and innovation and usually do not carry productized implementation to an existing specification; this occupation takes engineering implementation and maintenance as its object.
People willing to do algorithm and model research and experiments suit that direction; people willing to do implementation and testing and maintenance suit this occupation.
Mainly research plans and experiments and papers and prototype records.
Computer and information research scientists

Computer support specialists focus on user and desktop-level support and account and device handling and usually do not carry application code writing and testing; this occupation takes code and scripts as its object.
People willing to do user and desktop support suit that direction; people willing to do code writing and defect fixing suit this occupation.
Mainly tickets and equipment and account handling records.
Computer support specialists

Computer network architects focus on end-to-end network design and capacity and evolution planning and usually do not carry application layer code implementation; this occupation takes coding and validation of applications and scripts as its object.
People willing to do network architecture and capacity planning suit that direction; people willing to do application coding and testing suit this occupation.
Mainly architecture and design review and change and rollback records.
Computer network architects

The software quality assurance and testing direction focuses on test strategy and use cases and automation and defect tracking, and connects with this occupation on validation and defects, but leans more toward quality systems and test engineering; this occupation leans more toward functional implementation and debugging and maintenance.
People willing to do test strategy and quality systems suit that direction; people willing to do functional implementation and defect localization suit this occupation.
Mainly test plans and use cases and defects and quality report records.
Software quality assurance and testing direction

Moving from this occupation to an adjacent direction usually requires adding new capabilities and experience: the management direction needs people and budget and delivery management experience; the systems analysis direction needs business modeling and requirements engineering experience; the research direction needs algorithm and experiment and research method experience; the support direction needs scale experience in user and desktop and account services; the network architecture direction needs end-to-end topology and capacity modeling experience; the testing direction needs test strategy and automation and quality system experience. Coding and debugging and version management capabilities can transfer, but the scope of responsibility and authority of each direction must be re-established.

Roles that carry specification clarification and design

Specification misunderstandings or incomplete consideration of inputs and outputs and boundaries and exceptions cause rework in implementation and acceptance and may cause data errors and externally visible functional failures.

Turn the specification into a list of inputs and outputs and constraints and boundary conditions and exception scenarios and have the owner confirm; read the existing code and interfaces and data models and conventions before designing; clarify ambiguities and contradictions in writing and keep records.

Starting work directly from understanding; implementing only the normal path without considering exceptions; building a separate set of interfaces and structures inconsistent with existing conventions.
Roles that carry coding and debugging and validation

Insufficient validation and regression or poor assessment of the change scope lets hidden defects reach production and trigger under specific inputs and concurrency conditions, causing data corruption and online failures.

Write reproducible validation steps or use cases for the change and keep the execution results; confirm existing functionality still works after regression and assess the scope of impact; for parts that cannot be validated automatically, write out the manual validation steps and criteria.
Committing after only running it locally; only checking that the error disappeared without investigating the root cause; large refactoring without regression; swallowing exceptions to mask problems.
Roles that carry review and release and configuration responsibility
Bypassing review to merge directly, or directly changing production configuration and data, cannot be traced back when a fault occurs and causes irreversible data and service impact.

Submit according to the employer's review and branching and merge and release process and respond to review comments; confirm permissions and approvals for changes involving data and credentials and configuration and keep change records; prepare a fallback plan and observation window for releases.
Skipping review to save time; writing credentials in code or configuration files; changing data directly in production without records.
Roles that carry data and credential and personal information handling responsibility
Using real data for local testing or uploading logs and source code and credentials to unauthorized channels causes personal information and trade secret leakage and compliance liability.

Editorial suggestion: use desensitized or synthetic data according to the data nature and the approved environment, and check desensitization effectiveness and permissions; credentials are managed under control according to the system and actual rules, and change / rotation conditions are checked separately without setting a uniform cycle.

Avoid copying production data to unauthorized environments or leaking logs / credentials; account / credential changes are checked against the actual system and leakage situation, and a fixed rotation cycle is not used to judge all risks.
Roles that carry documentation and handover responsibility
Incomplete comments and documentation and version records make it impossible to restore design intent and scope of impact at staff changes and fault tracing and requirement changes.

Write key assumptions and boundaries and known limitations into comments and design notes; update workflow diagrams and user manuals and handover notes in step; let the colleague taking over understand and run and modify the program from the documentation.
Handing over verbally only; documentation inconsistent with the actual implementation; leaving known defects and temporary solutions unmarked.
Roles that carry external dependency and third-party component responsibility
Introducing unevaluated third-party components or outdated dependencies brings license and security vulnerability and maintenance interruption risk.

Before introducing a dependency, evaluate the license and maintenance status and known vulnerabilities; register dependencies and versions according to organizational systems and review regularly; prepare replacement or isolation plans for critical dependencies.
Copying code from the internet without checking the license; never updating dependencies; having no contingency for component deprecation.

values: Fictional task: for a fictional specification, complete the input and output and boundary and exception checklist, the design note and implementation and testing and debugging, and write the validation steps and results and known limitations and commit message.

Fictional materials: a fictional business specification (including one mutually contradictory acceptance condition and one unstated boundary case) and a piece of existing fictional code with its interface and naming and layering conventions.
Fictional conditions: a fictional review and branching and release process and a fictional data and credential and log handling requirement.
Fictional constraints: a fictional iteration cycle and available hours and existing dependency and third-party component list.

Step one: write out the specification breakdown and clarification checklist (list inputs and outputs and constraints and boundary conditions and exception scenarios, and mark the doubtful points needing confirmation from the specification owner).

Step two: write out the design note and implementation plan (explain consistency with existing structure and interfaces and naming conventions, new dependencies and scope of impact, and the error handling and logging strategy), and explain which changes need review and regression.

Step three: write out the validation and debugging and recording plan (including use cases and criteria and reproduction steps and regression scope and defect records and commit message and documentation updates), and explain which operations must be confirmed by release or security authorizers.
Reference deliverables: a specification breakdown and clarification checklist, a design note and implementation plan, and a validation and debugging and recording plan.

Evaluation basis: whether boundaries and exceptions are covered, whether the design is consistent with existing conventions, whether error handling and logging are clear, whether validation is reproducible and includes regression, whether commits and documentation are complete, and whether operations and data handling beyond authority are identified as requiring authorized confirmation.
Multiple reasonable approaches are allowed; if some information is judged insufficient, explicitly state which parts are insufficient and what additional information is needed.

All materials in this exercise are fictional and must not be run or change data in a real production environment, must not use real credentials or personal information, and must not serve as a basis for release or security or compliance decisions; real development and release must follow the applicable jurisdiction and employer systems and be carried out by roles with the corresponding authority and qualifications.
The specification and code and process and constraints given in the prompt are all fictional values, used only to practice breakdown and implementation and validation thinking.

A table: break each role requirement (education and professional foundation, programming and testing practical experience, development and testing training or certification, code review and release and production change authority, access and confidentiality requirements for data and credentials and logs, third-party component and license and security requirements) into 'condition - demonstrable experience - evidence location' line by line.
Evidence forms include desensitized design notes and commits and use cases and defects and release and scope of impact records, and training and authorization records.
For items without evidence, explicitly write 'to be added' and give a plan to fill the gap.

Review someone else's change plan (using fictional or desensitized materials), and list whether the elements you checked are complete (specification and boundaries and exceptions, consistency with existing conventions, error handling and logging, validation and regression, commits and documentation, data handling and permissions).
Write down where you disagree or need additions, and explain the basis.

Point out the parts of the plan that cannot be traced back (such as a missing boundary description or regression scope or scope of impact), and explain what consequences such gaps bring in online failures and audits.
A one-page change summary: goals and design trade-offs and validation results and residual risks and follow-up plan.
A boundary summary: your permission scope in this change and the matters you cannot commit to, and the matters that need confirmation by release or security or data authorizers.

A tools record: the purpose of the languages and frameworks and testing and version and continuous integration tools you used, and how you manage branches and versions and dependencies and configuration.
A collaboration note: how you communicate and keep records with the specification owner and testing and operations and peers.

The work context shown on this page: 100% use email every day, 90% sit continuously or almost continuously, and 64% consider being very exact or highly accurate extremely important.
entries.question: What does a computer programmer do every day?

entries.answer: Computer and information systems managers are responsible for the people and budget and delivery coordination of the information technology department; computer systems analysts focus on translating business requirements into system solutions and coordinating them; computer and information research scientists focus on algorithm and model research and innovation; computer support specialists focus on user and desktop-level support and account and device handling; computer network architects focus on end-to-end network design and capacity and evolution planning. This occupation focuses on writing and testing and maintaining code and scripts according to an established specification and usually does not carry final responsibility for product decisions or system architecture or research innovation. Shared capabilities do not mean the roles are interchangeable: the scope of responsibility and the authority differ. Note also that the adjacent occupational standard registered for Mainland China is the computer programmer (4-04-05-01), which can be used to explain the China skill boundary, but China-U.S. duties and qualifications or wages cannot be directly equated.

The core tasks of this occupation include clarifying intent from a vague specification, breaking down inputs and outputs and boundaries and exceptions, localizing defect root causes, and judging the scope of impact and whether to merge and release; these steps depend on engineering experience and responsibility. In addition, the ILO exposure index registered in this evidence route is only a task exposure measure, not a replacement rate or job reduction forecast. The more reliable uses of tools are code and comments and documentation and use case drafts and search and comparison. entries.question: Will AI replace computer programmers?

entries.answer: From the task structure, the earlier-affected parts are the structurable and digitizable steps: code drafts and refactoring suggestions and comments and commit messages, test case and documentation drafts, and searching and comparing existing code. The later-affected parts are the steps requiring judgment and responsibility: specification clarification and boundary and exception determination, defect root cause localization, and change scope judgment and merge and release decisions. It must be stressed that this judgment is editorial synthesis, not an exposure measure or job forecast provided by a source.

These capabilities depend on engineering experience and responsibility; replacing any of these steps with tool output makes the question of who is responsible for correctness and production results unanswerable.

subject.name: Computer programmer
subject.summary: Create, modify and test the code and scripts that make computer applications run, working from specifications written by software and web developers or other staff, and possibly develop and write computer programs to store and locate and retrieve specific documents and data: communicate with management and engineering and technical staff to clarify program intent; write and analyze and review and rewrite programs and prepare workflow charts and diagrams; correct errors by making appropriate changes and rechecking the program; perform or direct revisions and repair and expansion of existing programs; write and update and maintain computer programs or software packages; write development and revision documentation and insert comments; collaborate with operators or systems analysts to resolve problems; and train subordinates and users.
